title: Tech giants are fighting over talent

slides.headline: Tech giants are fighting over talent
slides.subtitle: From lawsuits to price hikes, here are the 5 tech stories you need to know today.

slides.headline: The Boring Company eyes $20B value
slides.explanation: Elon Musk’s tunneling startup is reportedly in talks to raise significant new funding. This valuation shows investors remain confident in the future of underground transit.

slides.headline: Warner Bros. sues Amazon over hiring
slides.explanation: Warner Bros. Discovery claims Amazon illegally poached its employees, including top marketing executives. It highlights the cutthroat competition for talent in the streaming wars.

slides.headline: OpenAI models were exposed online
slides.explanation: Reports show that certain OpenAI models were active on the internet for days before being secured. It is a reminder of how quickly security gaps can appear in fast-moving AI development.

slides.headline: Amazon faces breach of contract lawsuit
slides.explanation: Warner Bros. alleges that Amazon actively encouraged employees to break their existing contracts. This legal battle could change how tech and media giants recruit from each other.

slides.headline: Google hints at higher Pixel prices
slides.explanation: Google executives have suggested the next Pixel phone will cost more than the current model. The rising cost of hardware parts for AI is starting to hit consumer wallets.

caption:
The tech world is moving fast today, from high-stakes legal battles over employees to shifts in hardware pricing. Whether it's the race for AI talent or the cost of your next phone, these updates affect more than just the industry. Which of these stories do you think will have the biggest impact?

title: Global News in Five Quick Slides

slides.headline: Global News in Five Quick Slides
slides.subtitle: From wildfire crises to major protests, here is what is happening around the world.

slides.headline: Wildfires force mass evacuations in Europe
slides.explanation: Over 250,000 people have fled their homes as fires continue to burn across France and Spain. This is a critical situation as emergency crews struggle to contain the spreading flames.

slides.headline: Tensions rise with Houthi missile claim
slides.explanation: Houthi forces claim they launched a missile attack against Saudi Arabia. Meanwhile, the US military says it intercepted a tanker trying to bypass the American blockade on Iranian ports.

slides.headline: Bollywood stars face heat for silence
slides.explanation: Indian celebrities are being called out for not speaking up during massive youth protests. Public frustration is growing as major cultural figures stay quiet on the biggest demonstrations in years.

slides.headline: Ukraine drone strikes impact Russian retail
slides.explanation: Ukrainian drone attacks have targeted warehouses belonging to the Russian retailer Wildberries. These strikes are now causing real problems for the small businesses and consumers who rely on the platform.

slides.headline: Indian protests end after minister resigns
slides.explanation: The large scale protests against the Indian government have been called off following the education minister's resignation. This movement marked some of the strongest public pushback against the current administration in years.

caption:
The news moves fast, and it can be hard to keep track of what matters globally. We have broken down five major stories from today so you can stay informed in under a minute. Which of these stories do you think will have the biggest impact this week?
